articles.headline: China confirms trilateral summit between Xi, Trump, and Putin in Shenzhen
articles.title: China confirms first Xi-Trump-Putin summit on November 19
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping will host a trilateral meeting with United States President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on November 19, 2026, in Shenzhen, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Ministry. The historic gathering is expected to take place alongside Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation talks, though authorities did not specify the agenda items for the leaders.
articles.description: The Chinese Foreign Ministry gave no further details including about what the topics of the historic meeting in the southern Chinese city would be

articles.headline: Iran launches drone attack targeting US military base in Bahrain
articles.title: Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
articles.summary: Iran launched six drones at the al-Riffa air base in Bahrain, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, marking the second such attempt in three days. Bahrain's military stated that its air defense systems intercepted the attack before it achieved its objectives. The incident occurred amid ongoing tensions between Washington and Tehran concerning shipping security in the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: It marks the second attack on the country in three days and comes as the US and Iran remain locked in a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: US proposed Ukraine cede Donbas parts for NATO membership
articles.title: US suggested Ukraine cede parts of Donbas to Russia to become part of NATO
articles.summary: United States negotiators suggested that Ukraine surrender parts of eastern Donbas in exchange for joining the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Speaking in remarks released on Saturday, Zelenskyy stated he refused to cede territory but indicated he would hold a national referendum if comprehensive security guarantees and reconstruction funds were provided by international partners.
articles.description: Zelenskyy rejected the possibility of Ukraine committing to neutrality and said he refused to cede territory to Russia.

articles.headline: Trump considers holding off on further attacks against Iran
articles.title: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations, sources say
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump has told advisers that he may delay further military action against Iran if Tehran and its allies commit no new provocations, according to three sources. Regional leaders including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan urged the president during phone calls to avoid escalating the conflict further.
articles.description: The war has hiked global fuel prices and proven unpopular with U.S. voters, who handed control ‌of ⁠Congress to the Democrats in last week's midterm elections

articles.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week
articles.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin plan to hold a trilateral meeting next week during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, according to White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales. The leaders of the world's largest nuclear powers will discuss reducing nuclear weapons and the war in Iran, while bilateral talks are also scheduled between Trump and Xi.
articles.description: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.

articles.headline: Megaspeed launches internal investigation into business and supply chain
articles.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
articles.summary: Singapore-based Megaspeed announced an internal investigation into its business operations after executive Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy linked to Nvidia's former chief executive Jensen Huang, left her role in August 2025. The company stated it complies with all regulatory regimes, while US treasury and commerce officials face mounting congressional scrutiny over high-end AI chip exports.
articles.description: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.

articles.headline: US aviation authorities investigate nationwide ground stop caused by equipment failure
articles.title: After a nationwide ground stop, US faces aviation infrastructure questions
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration grounded United States flights for nearly four hours following a router malfunction during an upgrade performed by defence contractor L3Harris. Over 9,000 flights were cancelled and 1.5 million passengers stranded. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that investigations are ongoing into the incident, which has also renewed scrutiny regarding ageing infrastructure across the national aviation system.
articles.description: Trump has requested $50bn for upgrades, but Democratic lawmakers are asking for transparency before spending more.

articles.headline: India offers extended service terms to military recruits under Agnipath scheme
articles.title: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?
articles.summary: India's Ministry of Defence announced on 4 November that soldiers finishing four-year terms under the Agnipath programme can serve two additional years at higher pay. Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani stated the decision followed internal reviews. More than 18,300 recruits will complete their initial tenure by the end of 2026, amid ongoing debates regarding training duration and military effectiveness.
articles.description: India has softened its recruitment scheme, giving young soldiers a longer military stint and another shot at permanent service.

articles.headline: US proposes Ukraine cedes territory for NATO membership, says Zelensky
articles.title: U.S. proposes Ukraine cede territory in exchange for joining NATO: Zelensky
articles.summary: United States officials suggested for the first time that Ukraine should cede land to Russia in exchange for joining the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Moscow rejected an energy target ceasefire during talks in Abu Dhabi. He emphasized that any decision regarding territorial concessions would require societal approval following confirmation of security guarantees.
articles.description: Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had rejected a ceasefire on energy targets at talks in Abu Dhabi, as Moscow was “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold trilateral meeting at APEC summit
articles.title: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting at APEC: What to expect
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin will participate in their first trilateral meeting during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. Discussions will primarily address nuclear proliferation, notably the expired New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty. The gathering also occurs amid ongoing geopolitical tensions concerning conflicts in Ukraine and Iran alongside bilateral trade disputes.
articles.description: A nuclear treaty and the US's war on Iran are among priority topics for China, Russia and US leaders.

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces withdraw from Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend Aden
articles.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces announced a strategic withdrawal from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait area to prioritize the defense of Aden. The retreat on November 15, 2026, marks the end of a six-week counteroffensive against the Iran-aligned Houthis, who previously seized the Red Sea coast. Meanwhile, the International Committee of the Red Cross reported that the Houthis released 600 prisoners on the same day amid ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

articles.headline: Thousands of US flights face cancellations following technical failure
articles.title: Thousands of US flights still cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide
articles.summary: Thousands of US flights were cancelled or delayed after a technical failure in a communication router caused a national ground stop. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy stated normal operations may take time to recover as aircraft remain out of position. President Donald Trump urged Congress to approve funding to modernise the system.
articles.description: The US transport secretary says that normal air-traffic operations may not be restored until Monday.

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot calls for Benjamin Netanyahu's removal amid alleged election meddling
articles.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu can’t remain Israel PM amid alleged vote meddling
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot demanded the immediate departure of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following allegations of electoral interference reported by broadcaster Channel 12 on Sunday. The report claimed Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, improperly prompted police raids against Ra'am party members before the October 27 election. Netanyahu's Likud party condemned the remarks as outrageous incitement.
articles.description: Arab party members were reportedly arrested before Israeli elections based on unfounded evidence from the PM's office.

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone strike kills three in Russia amid NATO territory claims
articles.title: Three killed in Russia as Ukraine claims US floated NATO membership option
articles.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack killed a family of three in the Russian border region of Belgorod, according to local authorities. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed that United States negotiators raised the possibility of ceding eastern territory for North Atlantic Treaty Organization membership during recent talks in Abu Dhabi, though Kyiv rejected any immediate withdrawal from the Donbas region.
articles.description: Zelenskyy says the US asked for the first time whether Kyiv would cede land to Moscow in exchange for the NATO bid.

articles.headline: US media implicates former Indian intelligence chief in Pannun plot
articles.title: U.S. media names Indian official who allegedly ordered plot on Gurpatwant Singh Pannun
articles.summary: United States authorities assessed that an alleged assassination plot against Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun was directed by the former chief of India's Research and Analysis Wing, Samant Goel. According to a report by the Washington Post, officials believe the operation received official sanction from individuals connected to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration. The Indian Ministry of External Affairs declined to comment on the allegations.
articles.description: According to Washington Post, R&AW official Vikash Yadav directed businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic, to hire a hitman to kill Pannun outside his New York residence; it says NSA Ajit Doval was ‘probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists’

articles.headline: Nvidia must hire outside chief executive after Huang departure, Bessent says
articles.title: Bessent says Nvidia must ‘go outside the company’ to find new CEO
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Nvidia must hire an outside chief executive following the resignation of Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down on November 12, 2026, amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. Bessent added that the board and outside counsel must answer questions regarding export compliance within 10 days.
articles.description: U.S. Treasury ‌Secretary Bessent also said Nvidia’s board and outside counsel needed to answer, within the next 10 days, questions about the company’s culture ‌of compliance with export restrictions

articles.headline: Protests erupt in Gopalganj over proposed return of ousted leader Hasina
articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.summary: Supporters of ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina staged violent demonstrations in Gopalganj on November 15, 2026, demanding her return from India. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia in November 2025 for crimes against humanity. The unrest prompted the government to withdraw local officials and deploy paramilitary forces to maintain public order.
articles.description: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

articles.headline: Four nations urge Israel to allow immediate humanitarian aid into Gaza
articles.title: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urge Israel to allow aid into Gaza
articles.summary: Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom urged Israel to permit immediate and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza following severe floods. articles.headline: Israel restricts aid entry as winter storms batter Gaza
articles.title: Who can force Israel to implement Gaza ceasefire deal?
articles.summary: Palestinians in Gaza face harsh winter weather in tents without basic services while Israel restricts humanitarian aid entry. Calls from the United Nations, European Union and the US-established Board of Peace have gone unanswered, leaving displaced families vulnerable to flooding and cold conditions, according to the report.

articles.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo remains uncontrolled
articles.title: Africa CDC says Ebola outbreak in DR Congo ‘still not under control’
articles.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to battle an uncontrolled Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo strain, recording over 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths since May. Africa CDC director-general Jean Kaseya stated that delayed detection, conflict and a funding shortfall have hindered containment efforts, though the World Health Organization is advancing clinical trials.
articles.description: 'If we don't stop this outbreak now, it would be the worst Ebola outbreak,' Africa ​CDC director says.

articles.headline: UN reports twenty five seafarers killed near Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: UN says 25 seafarers killed in, around Hormuz since US-Israel war on Iran
articles.summary: According to the United Nations, at least twenty five seafarers have died in maritime security incidents around the Strait of Hormuz since February, as reported during a Security Council briefing on Friday. Khaled Khiari, assistant secretary-general for the Middle East, Asia and the Pacific, stated that October recorded the highest monthly tally of incidents tracked by the International Maritime Organization. The disruptions have significantly increased global energy and transport costs amid an ongoing conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran.
articles.description: 'Situation cannot become new normal', says UN's Khaled Khiari, as Iran reports three more vessels hitting mines.

articles.headline: Ukraine President Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink speed restrictions
articles.title: Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink restrictions and be on 'right side of history'
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that military satellite internet speeds remain restricted, hindering efforts to intercept Russian attacks. Speaking on Sunday, Zelensky said terminals operated by Elon Musk's Starshield system lost connection at speeds exceeding 161km/h. Meanwhile, regional officials reported ongoing Russian strikes resulting in multiple fatalities across Ukrainian regions including Chernihiv and Luhansk, while Ukraine launched retaliatory drone attacks on industrial sites in Russia.
articles.description: The Ukrainian president says the slowed-down internet is making it difficult to stop Russian attacks.

articles.title: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
articles.summary: Lawmakers from both parties are pursuing stricter export rules on artificial intelligence chips following a scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy. Senate leaders and House Speaker Mike Johnson have called for congressional testimony and renewed support for legislative measures limiting chip exports to China.
articles.description: Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. articles.headline: Microsoft apologizes for global outage disrupting products for nearly 24 hours
articles.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after day-long global outage
articles.summary: Technology giant Microsoft issued a profound apology for a massive technical failure affecting Microsoft 365 products globally across more than seventy countries. The disruption began on Thursday and lasted nearly 24 hours, impacting operations for businesses, government services, and hundreds of millions of users worldwide before services steadily recovered by Friday afternoon following a network capacity upgrade.
articles.description: Efforts to address the underlying problem with Outlook, Teams and Copilot are complete, the tech firm says.

articles.headline: Estonia closes border crossings with Russia after attempted arson attack
articles.title: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker
articles.summary: Estonian authorities announced the closure of border crossings with Russia following an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems. Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated on Sunday that eight individuals were detained over the incident, which Tallinn attributes to Russian military intelligence. Latvian Interior Minister Janis Dombrava confirmed several arrests involving local citizens. Officials stated the measure aims to curb hostile activities and prevent sanctions circumvention by Moscow.
articles.description: Eight arrests made in connection with an attempted arson, which Tallinn says was ordered by Russian intelligence.

articles.headline: Southeast Asian leaders extend Myanmar ban over failure to implement peace plan
articles.title: Southeast Asian leaders denounce violence in Myanmar, extend ban on its leader
articles.summary: Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations meeting in Manila on Sunday extended a ban on Myanmar's leader attending regional summits. The bloc stated that the military-backed government in Myanmar has failed to comply with the 2021 five-point peace plan and continues to attack civilians. Under the restrictions, Myanmar may only be represented by lower-level career diplomats during the ongoing three-day summit addressing regional conflicts.
articles.description: ASEAN leaders proposed the plan in April 2021 to try to ease the violence that erupted after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi

articles.headline: India health expenditure triples as household out-of-pocket spending declines
articles.title: India’s health spending triples to ₹4.14 lakh crore, but out-of-pocket share drops to 42.7%: NHA
articles.summary: India's Union government health expenditure increased from ₹1.30 lakh crore in 2013-2014 to ₹4.14 lakh crore in 2023-2024, according to National Health Accounts estimates. The Health Ministry reported that the proportion of out-of-pocket spending by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over the decade. The data highlights expanded public financing, increased primary healthcare spending, and growth in government and private health insurance schemes across the country.
articles.description: The share of healthcare costs borne by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over a decade, while social security spending on health rose from 6% to 11%

articles.headline: World Health Organisation warns of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza
articles.title: Respiratory illnesses rise in Gaza with worst to come as winter floods arrive, WHO says
articles.summary: The World Health Organisation reported that acute respiratory infections in Gaza have risen by 33,000 cases compared to last year. Dr Reinhilde Van De Weerdt stated that heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians, worsening overcrowding and living conditions. The agency warned that the situation will deteriorate further during winter, while Israeli military agencies maintained that winterisation supplies and medical equipment have been facilitated into the region.
articles.description: Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher

articles.headline: India and U.S. agree on preferential market access for Indian goods
articles.title: India, U.S. agreed on preferential market access for Indian goods in America: Goyal
articles.summary: India and the United States have agreed that Indian goods will receive preferential market access with lower duties compared to competitor nations. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal announced the development on November 15, 2026, in Cairo. Both nations previously finalised a framework for the bilateral trade agreement's first phase in February, aiming to conclude the initial tranche by the end of the financial year.
articles.description: The deal was to be signed earlier, but changes in U.S. tariff landscape led to further negotiations on the agreement

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way summit in China
articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way summit in China

articles.description: White House says Trump plans to discuss the Iran war and nuclear arms at a meeting on the sidelines of APEC next week.

articles.headline: Iraqi government launches anticorruption crackdown in Jurf al-Sakhar
articles.title: Will Iraq’s oil smuggling crackdown disarm militias without a conflict?
articles.summary: The Iraqi government launched a sweeping anticorruption campaign targeting the Jurf al-Sakhar area, a stronghold of Iran-linked militias near Baghdad. The initiative involved dismissing nine senior officials and police chiefs to curb oil smuggling networks without triggering armed conflict. Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi coordinated with political leaders, including the Popular Mobilisation Forces, to weaken armed groups through economic pressure.
articles.description: Iraq has dismantled an alleged smuggling ring in Jurf al-Sakhar which could squeeze militias and avert internal strife

articles.title: Record number of migrants arrive in Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.summary: Spain declared a migration emergency in the Canary Islands after more than 9,000 people arrived in the Atlantic territory since November. Territorial Policy Minister Angel Victor Torres visited El Hierro to address the record surge. Meanwhile, the International Organization for Migration recorded at least 450 deaths on the Western African Atlantic route during the first ten months of 2026.
articles.description: New EU migration and asylum laws have largely failed to stem flow of migrants to Spain and its territories.

articles.title: How telecoms upgrade work sparked US flight chaos
articles.summary: The United States Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop that lasted more than four hours on Friday due to a communication issue affecting air traffic control centres. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy explained that analogue telecom switches and routers became overloaded with data, causing thousands of flight delays and cancellations in the longest nationwide stoppage since September 11, 2001.
articles.description: US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading and not a cyber-attack.

articles.headline: U.S. flights grounded nationwide due to telecommunications outage
articles.title: U.S. flights resume after hours-long outage as FAA lifts nationwide ground stop
articles.summary: All departing flights across the United States were grounded on Friday, November 13, 2026, following a temporary telecommunications outage affecting air route traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration ordered the rare national stop out of an abundance of caution, stranding tens of thousands of passengers and causing widespread travel disruption. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin confirmed there was no indication of a nefarious attack.
articles.description: Disruption not due to a cyberattack or a sweeping Microsoft outage, top officials said; the incident marked only the second time such an alert was given in U.S. airspace since the 9/11 attacks

articles.headline: SpaceX catches giant Starship rocket booster mid-air in Texas
articles.title: ‘Almost magic’ as SpaceX craft caught mid-air: Why it matters
articles.summary: SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket using mechanical arms at Launch Pad 2 in Starbase, Texas. Aerospace engineers and NASA officials praised the achievement as a historic milestone for reusable space technology. The milestone follows 14 orbits over 22 hours and aims to reduce the costs of future lunar and Martian exploration missions significantly.
articles.description: SpaceX's Starship successfully returned to its launchpad after orbiting in space.

articles.headline: Gaza families bury loved ones recovered from rubble after years
articles.title: Gaza families bury bodies of loved ones trapped for years under rubble

articles.description: The remains of 69 Palestinians have been recovered in northern Gaza, allowing families to bury them.

articles.title: Starshield restrictions help Russia’s energy attacks on Ukraine: Zelenskyy
