articles.summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,531 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by a one-time exceptional charge of Rs 6,738 crore and Jaguar Land Rover restructuring. Despite the loss, overall revenue rose thirty-five percent year-over-year to Rs 96,340 crore, supported by record domestic sales exceeding 200,000 units.
articles.description: The figures are not comparable because last year the company had exceptional gains due to the demerger of the company. During the period, the company’s revenue increased to ₹96,340 crore from ₹71,414 crore in the year ago period, up 35% YoY

articles.headline: Narendra Modi says tribal communities suffered most due to Maoist violence
articles.title: ‘Escaping extreme poverty and Naxalism has improved tribal lives’, says PM Modi
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed a tribal pride programme in Gadchiroli, stating that tribal populations suffered severely and lost voting rights under previous administrations due to Maoist violence. He highlighted recent developmental initiatives, including the inauguration and foundation laying of projects worth approximately 30000 crore rupees across multiple states.
articles.description: PM cites World Bank report to claim that 50 crore Indians have escaped extreme poverty over last 12 to 13 years; says 125 districts were Naxal-affected in 2014, as previous regimes closed their eyes to the problem

articles.headline: UN says Israeli policies worsened deadly impact of Gaza winter storm
articles.title: UN says Israeli policies worsened deadly impact of Gaza winter storm
articles.description: The UN says Israel could have prevented death and destruction caused by the storm in Gaza had it allowed sufficient aid.

articles.headline: Hundreds of thousands protest Czech public media funding changes
articles.title: Czechs gather in big numbers to reject government's plan to overhaul funding of public media
articles.summary: Massive crowds rallied at Prague's Letná Park on November 15, 2026, to denounce Prime Minister Andrej Babis and his coalition's plan to overhaul public broadcaster funding, which critics warn threatens media freedom. According to lead organizer Mikulas Minar from the Million Moments for Democracy group, approximately 350,000 demonstrators attended. The controversial legislation would replace license fees with state budget funding and reduce budgets by fifteen percent.
articles.description: The massive protest took place at the capital's Letná Park, where huge crowds gathered during the 1989 Velvet Revolution, which ended more than 40 years of communist rule in the country

articles.headline: Karnataka government notifies amended BMLTA Act to protect infrastructure projects
articles.title: BMLTA Amendment notified: Tunnel Roads, Elevated Corridors to evade institutional scrutiny
articles.summary: The Karnataka government notified the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority Amendment Act on October 9, 2026, retrospectively shielding urban transport projects initiated between 2022 and mid-2026 from institutional scrutiny. Passed during the August monsoon session without debate, the legislation incorporates a controversial savings clause that exempts initiatives like tunnel roads and elevated corridors from the transport planning authority, drawing sharp criticism and pending legal challenges from civic groups.

articles.headline: Judge halts Trump administration closure of Washington DC golf course
articles.title: Judge blocks Trump closure of 'Trash Island' Washington DC golf course on Sunday
articles.summary: US District Judge Ana Reyes issued a temporary restraining order preventing the federal government from closing the historic East Potomac Golf Links in Washington DC for renovations. Reyes ruled that the administration violated federal laws to meet an arbitrary deadline and acted in bad faith, scheduling the order to remain in effect until November 28 while legal proceedings continue.
articles.description: The temporary order is part of a months-long challenge to the US president's plans to upgrade East Potomac Golf Links into a championship course.

articles.headline: Brinda Karat criticizes Modi government over agricultural and corporate policies
articles.title: Modi govt. implementing policies to hand over agri sector to corporates: Brinda Karat
articles.summary: Communist Party of India Marxist leader Brinda Karat accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration on November 15, 2026, of enacting policies that surrender the agricultural sector to domestic and foreign corporate entities. Speaking at the thirty sixth All India Kisan Sabha meeting in Nalgonda, she criticized soaring commodity prices, land acquisitions displacing indigenous Adivasi communities, and agreements with the United States that harm farmers, while urging Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy to protect constitutional rights.
articles.description: Centre systemically weakening Constitution and its institutions, she alleged

articles.headline: Uniform sugarcane pricing is impractical for factories, says Satish Jarkiholi
articles.title: All sugar factories cannot pay same price to farmers, says Satish Jarkiholi
articles.summary: Karnataka sugar factory owner and minister Satish Jarkiholi stated that uniform sugarcane pricing is impractical due to varying financial health, crop quality, and sugar recovery rates among factories. Speaking in Belagavi, he noted that base prices were set at 3,600 rupees per tonne following discussions with farmers, while urging the Union government to increase the minimum selling price of sugar.
articles.description: Union government should revise Minimum Selling Price of sugar, according to the Minister

articles.headline: Revanth Reddy urges Prime Minister Modi to expedite Telangana irrigation projects
articles.title: Revanth urges Modi to expedite clearances for Telangana irrigation projects
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi to request assistance in resolving inter-State water disputes and securing pending clearances for regional irrigation projects. The Chief Minister sought Maharashtra's consent for the Tummidihatti project and requested an additional 5,000 billion rupees under a special capital investment scheme to complete near-finished infrastructure developments.
articles.description: Seeks Centre’s intervention to secure Maharashtra’s approval for Tummidihatti project; requests ₹5,000 crore under SASCI; invites PM to Khelo India Youth Games

articles.headline: Leaders demand probe into deaths of two special police officers
articles.title: Congress demands probe into two SPOs’ death in Kishtwar; BJP claims their remains were ‘dishonoured’
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir political parties demanded an investigation on November 15, 2026, into the circumstances surrounding the deaths of Special Police Officers Babi Chand and Rashpal Kumar in Kishtwar. While opposition leaders questioned whether the officers were mistakenly shot by the Army or targeted by militants, the Bharatiya Janata Party alleged that the bodies were treated disrespectfully during transport, prompting demands for a comprehensive inquiry into the incident and subsequent police strategy.
articles.description: Political parties raise questions about the death of the two men on November 12, with the J&K Police having not yet issued a statement on the matter

articles.headline: Flames engulf Syrian refugee camp in eastern Lebanon
articles.title: Flames engulf Syrian refugee camp in eastern Lebanon
articles.description: A fire tore through a Syrian refugee camp in Bar Elias, eastern Lebanon.

articles.headline: South Eastern Railway probes empty Vande Bharat train journey with faulty brakes
articles.title: Empty Vande Bharat train travels 463 km with faulty brakes in Ranchi division
articles.summary: The South Eastern Railway zone initiated an investigation after an empty Vande Bharat train travelled 463 km from Jharkhand to Uttar Pradesh with isolated braking systems. Railway staff and crew members allegedly ignored multiple warnings from loco pilots regarding poor brake performance before the issue was identified at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya station. Officials cited widespread staff negligence during the October journey.
articles.description: Railway staff allegedly failed to ensure proper integration of the Vande Bharat's braking system with that of the goods locomotive which was to pull the rake through out the journey

articles.headline: BJP leader demands apology from Rahul Gandhi over Bharat Summit
articles.title: BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of treason over Bharat Summit
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party Telangana president N. Ramchander Rao demanded an unconditional apology from opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on November 15, 2026, accusing him of treason and inviting foreign anti-national groups to the Bharat Summit. Rao claimed the event allowed foreign interference in internal political affairs and defended the cancellation of a foreign journalist visa, while a union minister questioned the event expenditure.

articles.headline: CRPF withdraws anti-Naxal battalion from Chhattisgarh to deploy in Manipur
articles.title: CRPF withdraws anti-Naxal battalion from Chhattisgarh for Manipur duties
articles.summary: The Central Reserve Police Force withdrew more than one thousand personnel from anti-Naxal operations in Sukma district to bolster security forces in Manipur, marking the first such de-induction since the government declared the end of armed Maoism. Local police warned the move creates an operational vacuum, though officials stated similar troop reassignments may follow to strengthen regional borders.
articles.description: A battalion of more than 1,000 personnel based in Sukma has been sent to Manipur, with a proposal to withdraw at least three more from Chhattisgarh and Odisha, officials told PTI

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister urges central team to submit cyclone report
articles.title: Cyclone damage: Andhra Pradesh CM urges Central team to submit report in 10 days; State puts total loss at ₹2,484 crore
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu urged a central inspection team led by Chittaranjan Das to submit its assessment report within ten days and release immediate financial assistance following Cyclone Murasu. State assessments placed total losses at ₹2,484.43 crore across multiple sectors, prompting calls for permanent infrastructure solutions and targeted relief for affected agricultural communities.

articles.headline: Defence minister urges adoption of advanced technologies in non-destructive testing
articles.title: Rajnath Singh calls for AI, robotics in Non-Destructive Testing to strengthen defence sector
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged professionals on November 15, 2026, to adopt artificial intelligence, machine learning, and robotics in non-destructive testing to enhance India's defence ecosystem and achieve strategic self-reliance. Addressing a conference in Hyderabad, he emphasized that indigenous systems must meet strict reliability standards and called for domestic solutions tailored to national industrial requirements.

articles.headline: Rajnath Singh calls for indigenous development of advanced inspection technologies
articles.title: India should become innovator, global leader in advanced tech: Rajnath Singh
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged India to transition from a technology user to a global leader in non-destructive testing and aerospace evaluation during a conference in Hyderabad on November 15, 2026. He stressed that stringent quality assurance and indigenous development of advanced sensors and artificial intelligence are essential for securing defense supply chains and ensuring operational reliability.
articles.description: Defence Minister calls for strengthening India’s indigenous Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) capabilities

articles.headline: Tanker ship collides with docked river cruise boat in New Orleans
articles.title: All passengers, crew on New Orleans cruise ship survive crash with tanker on Mississippi River
articles.summary: A tanker vessel collided with the river cruise boat American Heritage while it was docked near the port of New Orleans on Friday. The collision involved approximately 130 passengers on board and left the pleasure vessel partially submerged and listing. Local emergency services responded with rescue operations, though the precise cause of the collision and the extent of any injuries remained unclear immediately.
articles.description: Tanker owned by subsidiary of Chinese shipbuilder; too early to tell what might have caused the crash, but videos indicate some kind of catastrophic system failure on the vessel, a maritime law expert said

articles.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu renews unity government appeal to Gadi Eisenkot
articles.title: Can Netanyahu and Eisenkot form a ‘unity’ government in Israel?
articles.summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu urged opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a national unity government in Israel. While Eisenkot dismissed the proposal as a bluff, both sides acknowledged ongoing discussions. President Isaac Herzog granted Eisenkot until December 6 to establish a coalition, navigating complex alliances in the Knesset involving ultra-Orthodox and Arab-led factions.
articles.description: Yashar and Likud are scheduled to hold talks on Sunday, but will need to overcome major differences to work together.

articles.headline: Global Microsoft outage disrupts businesses and services worldwide
articles.title: Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact
articles.summary: A global Microsoft disruption affecting Exchange Online and related services impacted businesses and public services worldwide on November 12 and 13, 2026. Indian enterprises, airlines, and international agencies experienced email and customer support delays. Microsoft reported recovery progress across affected infrastructure and stated it is investigating the root cause while addressing extensive message backlogs.
articles.description: Disruption to Microsoft’s cloud-based email service affects business operations and airline customer support in India; public services in several countries also report problems

articles.headline: Explosive attack targets investigative journalist’s home in Panama
articles.title: Explosive attack targets investigative journalist’s home in Panama
articles.description: An investigative journalist’s home in Panama was attacked in a suspected bombing.

articles.headline: Alice Huang visited Taiwan eight times during 2024 and 2025
articles.title: Alice Huang, accused of spying on Nvidia chief, entered Taiwan eight times in 2024-25: Official
articles.summary: Alice Huang, an executive accused of spying for Beijing while linked to Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, entered Taiwan eight times between 2024 and 2025 using a Hong Kong passport, according to Mainland Affairs Council Minister Chiu Chui-cheng on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Taiwanese officials stated she entered under standard business visitor status and security agencies are currently investigating the matter.
articles.description: Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory

articles.headline: Kayla Harrison defeats Amanda Nunes to retain Ultimate Fighting Championship bantamweight title
articles.title: Kayla ⁠⁠Harrison defeats Amanda Nunes to retain UFC bantamweight belt
articles.summary: American fighter Kayla Harrison defended her Ultimate Fighting Championship bantamweight title by defeating Amanda Nunes via a fourth-round submission at Madison Square Garden in New York. Harrison utilised her superior grappling skills to overcome the former two-weight champion. In the co-main event, French fighter Ciryl Gane secured a unanimous decision victory over American Josh Hokit to retain the heavyweight title.
articles.description: Harrison won by a fourth-round submission against MMA legend Nunes, who made a comeback after a three-year absence.

articles.headline: Aid agencies struggle to help more than 50,000 Ethiopian refugees in Kenya
articles.title: Aid agencies struggle to help more than 50,000 Ethiopian refugees in Kenya
articles.description: Aid agencies are struggling to provide food, medical care and shelter to more than 50,000 Ethiopian refugees in Kenya.

articles.headline: Two suspects arrested in Gurdaspur for Rajasthan railway track blast
articles.title: Two held in Rajasthan railway track blast case; police cite Pakistani handler links
articles.summary: Police arrested Mahakdeep Kaur and Devendra Singh in Gurdaspur during a joint operation by the Rajasthan Anti-Terrorism Squad and local law enforcement. Investigators indicated the suspects have links to Pakistani handlers and carried out a November 3 explosion on a railway track in Ramsinghpur using timer bombs supplied from across the border.
articles.description: Two people were arrested from Punjab’s Gurdaspur over the November 3 blast in Ramsinghpur, and police say they allegedly acted on instructions from Pakistan-based handlers

articles.headline: Australia defeat New Zealand to claim fourth Women’s Rugby League World Cup
articles.title: Australia crush New Zealand to win fourth Women’s Rugby League World Cup
articles.summary: Winger Jaime Chapman scored a hat-trick as Australia defeated New Zealand thirty-four to ten on Sunday in Brisbane to secure their fourth consecutive Women’s Rugby League World Cup title. The Jillaroos established a commanding thirty-four to six halftime lead before humid conditions slowed the match. New Zealand captain Raecene McGregor vowed her team would return stronger after the defeat.
articles.description: Australia dominated the first half and capitalised on the Kiwi Ferns’ errors to win 34-10 and clinch the trophy.

articles.headline: Microsoft services begin recovering after global outage
articles.title: Microsoft services begin recovering after global outage
articles.description: Microsoft services began recovering on Friday after a global outage disrupted Outlook and Teams.

articles.headline: Guatemala declares thirty-day state of emergency in eastern departments
articles.title: Guatemala declares state of emergency in east over drug violence
articles.summary: Guatemalan authorities declared a thirty-day state of emergency on Saturday in Zacapa and Izabal to combat drug violence following the killing of a lawmaker. The decree allows security forces to disperse groups by force and enter homes without a warrant. The United States designated the dominant local cartels as terrorist organisations on Friday.
articles.description: The 30-day decree covers Zacapa and Izabal, a week after Congressman Julio Portillo and three police officers were killed in an armed attack

articles.headline: Israeli forces seal Beit Ula industrial zone entrances
articles.title: Siege on Hebron’s Beit Ula industrial zone threatens Palestinian economy
articles.summary: Israeli forces sealed the Beit Ula industrial zone entrances with earth barriers on November 4, isolating sixty Palestinian businesses and threatening two thousand five hundred jobs. Daily sales at Fayez al-Amleh’s door factory dropped drastically following the closure. Palestinian officials condemned the measures as collective punishment and economic warfare against the West Bank.
articles.description: Israel takes measures to crush Palestinian business in the occupied West Bank.

articles.headline: Mansour Abbas faces pressure over Hamas recognition in coalition talks
articles.title: Israel coalition talks put Arab party leader under pressure over Hamas
articles.summary: Mansour Abbas faced political pressure as prospective Israeli prime minister Gadi Eisenkot demanded he recognise Hamas as a terrorist organisation to join the coalition. Abbas denied making any declaration on Hamas during recent consultations. Inclusion of Ra’am’s eight seats could help Eisenkot secure a majority, though right-wing opposition remains a significant hurdle.
articles.description: Mansour Abbas faces mounting pressure from Israel’s change bloc to denounce Hamas as a prerequisite for coalition role.

articles.headline: Amazon plans World Product Graph to index global online shopping data
articles.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
articles.summary: Amazon is reportedly planning to build the World Product Graph, a comprehensive data vault containing information on products sold anywhere across the internet. According to Reuters, the initiative aims to reduce user reliance on platforms like Reddit and Google while improving the accuracy of Amazon’s shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping. Amazon stated that the internal document does not necessarily reflect current plans.
articles.description: Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn't sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters. The project, called the "World Product Graph," is meant to make it less likely that shoppers leave Amazon to do their […]

articles.headline: Two injured after passenger and cargo planes collide in Miami
articles.title: At least two injured as passenger, cargo planes collide at U.S. airport
articles.summary: Two people sustained minor injuries when a Copa Airlines passenger plane collided with a UPS cargo aircraft while taxiing at Miami International Airport on Saturday. The collision occurred at approximately 9:15 p.m. when the Boeing 737 wingtip struck the Boeing 767 nose. The Federal Aviation Administration is investigating the incident alongside both airlines.
articles.description: According to the report, all 166 passengers and six crew members disembarked, and the Copa aircraft returned to the terminal

articles.headline: Indian student protesters face heavy restrictions following summer demonstrations
articles.title: After a summer win, India's Gen Z protesters face a winter of uncertainty
articles.summary: Youth-led demonstrations in India have encountered severe police crackdowns and legal challenges as authorities move to curb dissent. Following a successful summer campaign that forced a federal minister's resignation, student activists now struggle to assemble. The governing party defends the restrictions, citing public order and legal boundaries, while legal experts and organizers warn that prolonged proceedings aim to deter opposition.
articles.description: A new wave of youth dissent swept India this summer, fuelled by frustration and irreverent online satire.

articles.headline: Jordanian court sentences three men to death for fatal church shooting
articles.title: Three men sentenced to death in Jordan over fatal church mass shooting
articles.summary: A Jordanian court sentenced three unidentified men to death by hanging for a mass shooting that killed nine people and injured 34 others at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate on 23 October. According to Jordan's Armed Forces, the convicted relatives were found guilty of terrorist acts and weapons possession following a shootout that led to their arrest three days after the attack.
articles.description: The attack on funeral at a Greek Orthodox church killed nine and injured 34 others last month.

articles.headline: Digital lending platforms pose hidden financial and personal data risks
articles.title: Need a quick loan? Beware of digital lending traps
articles.summary: Unsuspecting borrowers face severe hazards when utilizing online financial applications for rapid cash advances. According to reports published on November 16, 2026, instantaneous mobile funding methods frequently conceal excessive fees, unauthorized exploitation of private information, and aggressive harassment by debt collectors. This situation matters because individuals seeking fast capital often suffer unexpected financial and psychological harm from predatory digital lenders operating without adequate oversight.
articles.description: From hidden charges and misuse of personal data to coercive recovery tactics, digital borrowing demands more than a cursory glance as borrowers need to know what the loan really costs

articles.headline: India defeats Pakistan in Under-19 Asia Cup cricket final
articles.title: India’s Under-19 Asia Cup win over Pakistan marred by post-match aggression
articles.summary: India secured a nail-biting one-wicket victory against Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final at the Oman Academy Cricket Ground in Al Amerat. Lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva orchestrated a crucial ninth-wicket partnership to successfully chase a 338-run target. However, post-match celebrations were marred by aggressive on-field behavior from winning players toward their opponents.
articles.description: India beat Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling comeback in the final but follow it up with unsporting behaviour.

articles.headline: Delhi records very poor air quality with temperature dropping below average
articles.title: Air quality very poor in city; IIT Delhi records highest AQI of 428
articles.summary: Delhi recorded a very poor air quality index of 350, with the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi noting the highest reading at 428 according to the Sameer application. The India Meteorological Department reported a minimum temperature of 18.6 degrees Celsius on November 15, 2026, which was 5.1 degrees below the seasonal average, alongside high morning humidity levels of 91 per cent.
articles.description: Of the 54 monitoring stations, 47 recorded 'very poor' air quality, while seven were in the 'severe' category

articles.headline: Air purifier sales surge across India amid severe pollution
articles.title: Air purifier sales surge as Delhi-NCR AQI deteriorates; demand spreads beyond traditional markets
articles.summary: Retailers and manufacturers across India report doubled sales volumes for air purifiers following severe pollution spikes in the Delhi National Capital Region, where the average air quality index reached 367 on Saturday. Companies such as Croma and Amazon India noted expanding demand beyond traditional metropolitan markets. Industry forecasts project substantial growth as consumers increasingly adopt air purification devices as year-round health necessities.
articles.description: The segment, earlier considered to be a niche and largely confined to top metropolitan cities, is now witnessing demand from other parts of the country, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.

articles.headline: Three people arrested in Bhopal for digital arrest scam involving Delhi woman
articles.title: Three arrested in Bhopal for duping Delhi woman of ₹71 lakh in ‘digital arrest’ scam
articles.summary: Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations unit of the Delhi Police arrested three individuals from Bhopal on November 15, 2026. The suspects allegedly impersonated an Indian Police Service officer and duped a Delhi woman of 71 lakh rupees through intimidation in a digital arrest scam. Authorities recovered three newly purchased mobile phones while investigation into the broader network continues.
articles.description: The accused impersonated an IPS officer and threatened the victim with arrest in a fake ₹6.5-crore money laundering case; IFSO uncovers a network of mule bank accounts used to route the cheated money

articles.headline: Cape Verde votes in presidential election focusing on persistent emigration
articles.title: Polls open in Cape Verde in race with first female presidential candidate
articles.summary: Voters in Cape Verde are casting ballots in a presidential election featuring six candidates, including incumbent Jose Maria Neves and opposition challenger Joana Rosa, who is the first female candidate in the nation's history. The election centers on addressing high emigration driven by a lack of jobs. Over 300,000 citizens are eligible to participate, with results expected within three days.
articles.description: Joana Rosa and four other opposition candidates face off against President Jose Maria Neves, who wants a second term.

articles.headline: Pope Leo addresses community hardship during remote Andean town visit
articles.title: Pope Leo speaks of community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes town
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV visited the isolated Andean village of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba in northern Peru, addressing local suffering caused by poverty, declining birth rates, and forced migration. During an outdoor Mass attended by thousands, the US-born pontiff reflected on his previous tenure as bishop in the region before continuing his twelve-day Latin American tour.
articles.description: Santa Cruz de Succhabamba is part of the Diocese of Chiclayo, where the Pope served as bishop from 2015 to 2023.

articles.headline: Telugu Desam Party-led alliance wins 12 of 13 mayoral posts in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh local body polls: TDP-led NDA wrests 12 of 13 Mayor posts; Anantapur only solace for YSRCP
articles.summary: The Telugu Desam Party-led National Democratic Alliance secured twelve out of thirteen mayoral positions and nearly two-thirds of wards in urban local body elections across Andhra Pradesh on November 4, 2026. The results dealt a blow to the YSR Congress Party, which won only the Anantapur mayoral post. Polling covered thirteen municipal corporations and eighty-seven municipalities amid disruptions from two cyclones.
articles.description: TDP wins 2,571 of 3,897 wards for which poll results have been declared, while YSRCP secures 550 wards, JSP emerges victorious in 484 wards, and BJP grabs 153 wards; counting for Chirala municipality postponed to November 6

articles.headline: Protesters condemn US policies as ASEAN summit begins in Manila
articles.title: Protesters condemn US policies as ASEAN summit begins in Manila
articles.description: Southeast Asian leaders arriving in the Philippines for the ASEAN summit have been met with protests.

articles.headline: Low-pressure area forms over southeast Bay of Bengal
articles.title: Low-pressure area forms over Bay of Bengal, likely to intensify into depression by November 15
articles.summary: A low-pressure area has formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal and is expected to intensify into a depression by November 15, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department. The system developed under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation and is predicted to bring squally weather and strong winds to the Andaman Sea and surrounding regions.
articles.description: The system formed at 5:30 a.m. under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the central Andaman Sea and adjoining Andaman and Nicobar Islands, according to the latest weather update

articles.headline: West Bengal legislative assembly representation analysed ahead of elections
articles.title: Minorities have been underrepresented in Bengal Assembly
articles.summary: The article is a partial text discussing the upcoming election process in West Bengal, India, where the Election Commission has placed nearly 60 lakh citizens under adjudication. It notes that candidate lists offer a lens to assess commitments to pluralistic social fabric, while evaluating the representation of various social groups in the seventeenth West Bengal Legislative Assembly.
articles.description: Despite its reputation as a progressive State, women and Muslims have sparsely held power in West Bengal

articles.headline: Deep ocean mission is crucial for India according to ministry secretary
articles.title: Deep Ocean Mission important for India’s future: MoES secretary
articles.summary: Srinivasa Kumar Tumalla, Secretary of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, has defended the Deep Ocean Mission, stating that current deep-sea mining activities are limited to exploratory surveys located thousands of kilometers away from the coast in the central Indian Ocean basin. According to the official, the initiative is vital for securing metals needed for electric vehicles and power grids.
articles.description: This is not done in the coastal area, but in the central Indian Ocean basin at water depths of about 5,000 metres. That’s very far from the coast., almost 2,500 km away, said Srinivasa Kumar Tumalla, MoES Secretary

articles.headline: Fifth Canadian soldier dies from injuries following military base fire
articles.title: Fifth Canadian soldier dies from injuries caused by large fire at military base
articles.summary: Private William Douglas Dal Bianco has died from injuries sustained during a grass fire that swept through Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta on October 17. The blaze, triggered by a live-fire training exercise, previously resulted in four deaths and injured thirty-eight military personnel. Prime Minister Mark Carney and military officials expressed their condolences following the soldier's death.
articles.description: Pte William Douglas Dal Bianco died from his injuries on Friday, a month after a fire that tore through CFB Wainwright.

articles.headline: COP31 talks face sluggish climate finance responses amid Western security pressures
articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.summary: Urgent demands for climate finance from vulnerable developing nations met a slow response at the COP31 summit in Antalya as Western governments prioritized national security and domestic living costs. Host country Turkiye and Australia focused on implementing existing pledges rather than setting new targets. While multilateral development banks reported record lending in 2025, analysts noted significant funding gaps driven by geopolitical tensions, constrained fiscal spaces, and high capital costs.
articles.description: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

articles.headline: Jordan court sentences three men to death over church attack
articles.title: Jordan sentences three men to death over church attack
articles.summary: A Jordanian court sentenced three men to death by hanging on November 15, 2026, for a deadly gun attack on a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud village that killed nine people and wounded 25 others on October 23. The State Security Court found the two Jordanian brothers and their relative guilty of terrorism and weapons offences.
articles.description: Gunmen killed nine people and wounded 25 others when they stormed a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud village, in Jordan's Karak governorate on October 23

articles.headline: Karnataka chief minister asserts state will build Mekedatu balancing reservoir project
articles.title: Mekedatu is Karnataka’s right, we will build dam and release Tamil Nadu’s share of water: D.K. Shivakumar
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar stated on November 14, 2026, that the state will proceed with the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project while continuing to provide Tamil Nadu with its mandated share of Cauvery water. Addressing opposition from neighbouring leaders, he defended the infrastructure plan as a state right and discussed related financial and transit proposals with central authorities.
articles.description: The Karnataka Chief Minister invites Tamil Nadu delegation to visit project site and understand its benefits rather than oppose it

articles.headline: Qatar and Turkiye send message of deterrence with new defence pact
articles.title: Qatar and Turkiye send message of deterrence with new defence pact
articles.description: Qatar and Turkiye have signed a mutual defence pact, deepening their partnership amid growing regional instability.

articles.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet enabling Dots agents to make purchases
articles.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence company OpenAI introduced a new wallet feature for its Dots agents, allowing the tools to make purchases on behalf of users. Rolling out to adult ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States using specific payment cards, the system requires biometric verification for every transaction and substitutes card details with payment tokens to protect financial data.
articles.description: After launching its Dots AI agents platform earlier this year, OpenAI is launching a wallet for the agents. ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting today for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and older using a US billing address and "eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa cards." After adding a card […]

articles.headline: Thousands in Portugal protest against surging rental prices
articles.title: Thousands in Portugal protest against surging rental prices
articles.description: Thousands of people across Portugal are angry about rising rental prices, demanding action to end the housing crisis.

articles.headline: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente denies country has racism problem
articles.title: De la Fuente denies racism in Spain despite Yamal, Vinicius avowals
articles.summary: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente claimed his country has no racism problem ahead of a UEFA Nations League match against England. His remarks followed recent Islamophobic chants punished by FIFA and public disclosures from players like Lamine Yamal and Vinicius Jr regarding recurring discrimination they faced within the country.
articles.description: Yamal and Vinicius have publicly said they face racist abuse in Spain, which has faced FIFA punishment over the issue.

articles.headline: Microsoft services recover gradually following widespread global communications outage
articles.title: Microsoft says services still returning amid widespread outage
articles.summary: Technology corporation Microsoft reported recovering email and communication services after a mass disruption affected seventy-four countries for more than twenty-four hours. The server overload impacted global businesses, governments, and millions of subscribers using Microsoft 365 products. While the incident prompted widespread logistical challenges and forced some institutions to use alternative methods, the company stated the issue was not caused by cyberattacks.
articles.description: Governments, businesses, individuals were disrupted globally as server failures stretch into second day.

articles.headline: South China Sea code of conduct pact unlikely during ASEAN summit
articles.title: Pact on South China Sea code of conduct unlikely, as ASEAN leaders gather
articles.summary: Negotiators have finalised 80 percent of a long-awaited Association of Southeast Asian Nations and China code of conduct for the South China Sea, but analysts state a final agreement is unlikely during the regional bloc summit in Manila. Department of Foreign Affairs Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro confirmed that geographical disputes remain among the contentious issues.
articles.description: Finishing negotiations for disputed South China Sea agreement will be a 'tall order', analysts say.

articles.headline: Indian student Bilal Kazi jailed for 30 years for online child abuse
articles.title: Indian student jailed for 30 years for online child sex abuse in U.K.
articles.summary: Bilal Kazi, a 27-year-old Indian student, was sentenced to 30 years in prison at Chester Crown Court on November 13, 2026, after pleading guilty to exploiting and coercing children online. U.K. authorities identified 70 victims targeted through social media and gaming platforms where Kazi posed as a teenage boy to build trust.
articles.description: The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh secures ₹9.88 lakh crore in investments at Vizag summit
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh secures ₹9.88 lakh crore investment commitments at CII Partnership Summit in Vizag
articles.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu announced that Andhra Pradesh attracted investment commitments worth ₹9.88 lakh crore through 303 memoranda of understanding during the 31st Confederation of Indian Industry Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam. Speaking on November 14, 2026, Naidu stated the government will introduce a retrospective Investment Protection Act to reassure businesses, aiming to generate approximately 3.49 lakh jobs across various sectors while boosting both industrial and agricultural development.
articles.description: A.P. government will implement Investment Protection Act with retrospective effect from 2024, says Chief Minister Naidu

articles.headline: Japan defeats Brazil three to two in international friendly match
articles.title: Japan stun Brazil 3-2 in stoppage time as Ancelotti, Raphinha sent off
articles.summary: Japan secured a three to two victory against Brazil at the National Stadium in Singapore after substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scored a stoppage time winner. Vinicius Junior had earlier erased a two goal deficit following strikes from Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti and forward Raphinha received red cards during protests following a video assistant referee review.
articles.description: Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s late goal helps Japan avenge their defeat by Brazil in the World Cup round of 32.

articles.headline: IRGC says tanker caught fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: IRGC says tanker caught fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: A liquefied gas carrier caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines, according to the IRGC.

articles.headline: Punjab National Bank promises to honour genuine claims in fund misappropriation case
articles.title: PNB fund misappropriation case: Bank says genuine claims to be honoured, FIR registered in Gr Noida
articles.summary: Punjab National Bank assured customers on October 29, 2026, that all legitimate claims will be honoured after nearly two dozen account holders reported missing funds exceeding 11 crore rupees at its Greater Noida branch. Police registered a first information report against unidentified employees for criminal breach of trust, and bank management suspended several staff members as investigations proceed.
articles.description: The bank said it was extending full cooperation to the authorities concerned and taking necessary steps to address the concerns of affected customers

articles.headline: Turkiye and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement in Istanbul
articles.title: Turkiye, Qatar sign mutual defence agreement, Turkish presidency says
articles.summary: Turkiye and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement on November 13, 2026, during a meeting in Istanbul between Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan and Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani. The Turkish presidency stated that the accord aims to foster regional peace and dialogue in the Gulf, building upon previous defense cooperation efforts involving other regional powers.
articles.description: Turkiye and Qatar were working to develop and diversify their energy partnership, and that their cooperation ‌in the defence industry would ​continue to grow, a statement from the Turkish presidency quoted President Erdogan as saying

articles.headline: Delhi Police arrest two sharpshooters planning attacks in Mumbai and Delhi
articles.title: How a Delhi extortion plot led police to Mad Sandhu murder accused who was planning attack on Amitabh Bachchan
articles.summary: Delhi Police arrested two alleged sharpshooters linked to a foreign-based gangster, foiling planned extortion attacks targeting a Bollywood actor and a businessman. Deputy Commissioner of Police Narra Chaitanya stated that Vikas Thakur and Deepak Singh were apprehended in separate intelligence-led operations. Interrogation revealed that Deepak Singh was instructed to target actor Amitabh Bachchan over purported remarks regarding the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.
articles.description: The Special Cell arrested two alleged shooters linked to a foreign-based gangster in separate operations in Delhi and Mumbai, foiling a planned shooting at a businessman and an alleged attack outside the Bollywood actor’s Mumbai residence

articles.headline: Kozhikode cyber fraud complaints exceed 2200 in ten months of 2026
articles.title: Cyber fraud reporting rises amid faster police interventions
articles.summary: Kozhikode city police recorded over twenty two hundred cyber fraud complaints in the first ten months of 2026, driven by rising public awareness and faster investigation mechanisms. Senior officials report that women account for about seventy percent of victims in these financial fraud cases, while dedicated help desks aim to freeze funds before withdrawal.
articles.description: Police officers involved in cybercrime investigations say the growing number of complaints is an indication of the public response to awareness campaigns and the grievance redressal measures; use of advanced cyber technologies and track fraudsters has further strengthened the investigation process, encouraging victims to report incidents at the earliest, they point out

articles.headline: Congress seeks to contest 181 seats in Uttar Pradesh assembly polls
articles.title: Congress wants to contest 181 seats in 2027 UP polls, indicates Akhilesh
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav stated that the Congress party wants to contest 181 seats in the upcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Speaking in Delhi, Yadav affirmed that the INDIA opposition bloc remains united to defeat the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party. He criticized the state government over exam paper leaks, infrastructure corruption, and alleged religious donation thefts at the Ayodhya Ram temple, while confirming plans to visit the temple himself.
articles.description: Asked if the demand was of 200 seats, he replied, "A little less than that." When the interviewer suggested 180 seats, Mr. Yadav said, "Add one more," indicating that the Congress has sought 181 seats from the SP

articles.headline: Depression over Bay of Bengal expected to become severe cyclonic storm
articles.title: No rainfall alerts for Andhra as depression to turn severe cyclonic storm over Bay of Bengal by November 17
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported that a low-pressure area over the Southeast Bay of Bengal intensified into a depression on November 15, 2026. Currently located hundreds of kilometres from Port Blair and Chennai, the system is projected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17. Authorities in Andhra Pradesh have not yet issued rainfall alerts for the system.
articles.description: At 5.30 a.m., the system lay centred over southeast and southwest Bay of Bengal, about 700 km west-southwest of Port Blair

articles.headline: NATO scales back high-level meetings and cancels planned Albania summit
articles.title: NATO to skip a leaders' summit in Albania next year as high-level meetings are scaled back
articles.summary: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is reducing high-level gatherings and canceled a planned leaders summit in Albania, citing internal disagreements regarding defense spending, Iran, and the war in Ukraine. Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama stated that no consensus exists for a 2027 summit in the country. Secretary-General Mark Rutte defended the decision while emphasizing the organization's flexibility and the high financial and security costs associated with hosting large member meetings.
articles.description: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte played down the issue. “We are flexible with NATO summits,” he said

articles.headline: Foreign investors pump 84290 crore into Indian equities in November
articles.title: FPIs pump ₹84,290 crore into equities in first fortnight of November
articles.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors injected eighty four thousand two hundred ninety crore rupees into Indian equities between November two and thirteen after consecutive monthly outflows. Analysts attribute the reversal to a global artificial intelligence selloff, falling crude prices, and attractive large cap valuations that helped the Nifty benchmark surpass twenty five thousand.
articles.description: According to the data, Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) made a net investment of ₹84,290 crore in Indian equities during November 2-13, covering nine trading sessions.

articles.headline: Bus and truck collision leaves 23 dead in Assam
articles.title: Students among 24 dead in bus-truck collision in Assam’s Kaziranga
articles.summary: At least twenty-three people were killed and twenty others injured following a head-on collision between a speeding minibus and a container truck on National Highway 715 near Kaziranga National Park in Assam. Local authorities and Assam minister Atul Bora oversaw rescue operations, transferring critically injured victims to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital for emergency treatment.
articles.description: Officials suspected that overspeeding by the minibus, travelling from Golaghat to central Assam’s Nagaon, caused the accident

articles.headline: Israel bars supplies needed to treat six-year-old Gaza burn victim
articles.title: Israel bars supplies needed to treat six-year-old Gaza burn victim
articles.description: Six-year-old burns victim Masa is one of the patients in Gaza whose recovery is under threat due to Israeli restrictions

articles.headline: Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves in Cape Verde presidential election
articles.title: Cape Verde could elect first woman President since gaining independence in 1975
articles.summary: Cape Verdeans may elect their first female president as former Justice Minister Joana Rosa opposes incumbent Jose Maria Neves in the election concluding on November 29, 2026, if a runoff occurs. The Atlantic island nation, with about half a million residents, faces economic challenges as young citizens seek opportunities abroad. According to political science professor Roselma Evora, Neves seeks to improve social services while Rosa advocates for a political counterweight against the governing party.
articles.description: Six candidates are competing, with a runoff scheduled for Nov. 29 if no candidate receives more than half the votes

articles.headline: United Nations Security Council holds straw polls to select new secretary-general
articles.title: Secret votes and vetoes: How will the next UN chief be picked?
articles.summary: The United Nations Security Council is conducting secret straw polls to recommend a successor to outgoing Secretary-General Antonio Guterres before December 31, 2026. Eight candidates are competing, including International Atomic Energy Agency head Rafael Grossi and UN Conference on Trade and Development chief Rebeca Grynspan. Permanent council members hold veto power over the final selection, which requires approval from the UN General Assembly.
articles.description: With no frontrunner for the job, eight candidates are vying for the UN Security Council's recommendation.

articles.headline: Two cattle smugglers killed in police encounter in Haryana
articles.title: Two cattle smugglers killed in encounter with police in Haryana
articles.summary: Two suspected cattle smugglers died and another sustained injuries during an exchange of gunfire with police in Nuh on November 15, 2026. The clash occurred when a Crime Investigation Agency team intercepted a pickup vehicle carrying seven cows. According to a Nuh police spokesperson, authorities recovered three country-made pistols and multiple cartridges, and a magisterial inquiry has been initiated into the incident.
articles.description: During the exchange of fire, three people sustained bullet injuries and were rushed to Nalhar Medical College. Two of the injured, identified as Sabir and Gabbar alias Hadiya, succumbed to their injuries, while Tahir is undergoing treatment

articles.headline: Voyager 1 approaches one light-day distance milestone in interstellar space
articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 closes in on a light-day in interstellar space for new distance record
articles.summary: NASA spacecraft Voyager 1 is nearing a historic milestone by reaching one light-day from Earth, marking a distance of more than 26 billion kilometres after 49 years in operation. Launched in 1977, the probe continues to transmit scientific data from interstellar space while project managers and space agencies celebrate the achievement with global tributes.
articles.description: NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star

articles.headline: India votes against UN General Assembly death penalty moratorium resolution
articles.title: India votes against UNGA resolution calling for global moratorium on death penalty
articles.summary: India joined several other nations in voting against a United Nations General Assembly draft resolution urging countries to establish a moratorium on the death penalty with the goal of abolishing it. The resolution, introduced by Mexico, was adopted on November 13, 2026, with 133 votes in favour, 33 against, and 16 abstentions. It expressed deep concern over a surge in reported executions during 2025.
articles.description: The resolution expressed deep concern that, despite the global trend towards limiting the application of the death penalty, there was a significant surge in reported executions in 2025.

articles.headline: Karnataka High Court urges security forces to review personnel mental health policies
articles.title: Karnataka High Court asks security, police organisations to review mental health policies for armed personnel
articles.summary: Justice Suraj Govindaraj of the High Court of Karnataka quashed criminal proceedings against a Central Industrial Security Force Sub-Inspector who attempted suicide in 2022. The court advised police and security organisations to examine mental health frameworks and provide confidential counselling. It cited the Mental Healthcare Act of 2017 to emphasize the severe stress faced by armed personnel.
articles.description: Justice Suraj Govindaraj passed the order while quashing the criminal proceedings against a 37-year-old CISF Sub-Inspector for attempting to kill herself in 2022 by using her service pistol while on duty in Mangaluru

articles.headline: Karnataka mandates school gynaecological check-ups and student safety measures
articles.title: Karnataka mandates gynaecological check-ups for girls, sex education in schools
articles.summary: The Karnataka government issued a joint circular mandating gynaecological check-ups for girls, sex education, and CCTV installations across all educational institutions. The guidelines establish Child Protection Committees, require the appointment of counsellors, and enforce legal action for negligence in child marriage or POCSO Act cases, following concerns that began in June 2025.
articles.description: Child Protection Committees, CCTV cameras, counselling and awareness programmes among measures mandated by joint circular

articles.headline: India and Egypt aim to expand bilateral trade and investment
articles.title: India, Egypt look to strengthen trade, investment ties, Piyush Goyal says
articles.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal announced during a visit to Cairo that India seeks to strengthen trade and investment ties with Egypt. Speaking to the Indian Community Association in Egypt on November 14, 2026, he noted that bilateral trade stood at approximately 6.5 billion dollars during the 2025-26 period, while leading a 132-member business delegation.
articles.description: Addressing a community event organised by the Indian Community Association in Egypt in Cairo, Piyush Goyal said the bilateral trade between the countries stood at about $6.5 billion

articles.headline: Bahrain interior ministry issues threat alerts following drone interception
articles.title: Sirens sound in Bahrain as Iran’s Guards claim drone attack
articles.summary: The Bahraini interior ministry published two alerts on the platform X urging residents and citizens to remain calm and seek safe locations. These warnings followed claims by Iran’s Revolutionary Guards regarding an attack on a United States radar in Bahrain, a claim denied by the United States military after it intercepted two Iranian drones without causing any harm.
articles.description: Bahrain, ⁠home to ⁠the U.S. Navy’s Fifth Fleet, urged citizens and ​residents to ‌remain calm and proceed to the nearest safe location, ‌its Interior Ministry ​said

articles.headline: Ukraine launches massive drone barrage as peace negotiators discuss European security
articles.title: Ukraine fires nearly 1,200 drones at Russia as U.S.-led talks consider wider European security
articles.summary: Ukraine fired nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its largest aerial attacks, according to Russia’s Defence Ministry, resulting in seven deaths and seventeen injuries across three regions. Simultaneously, United States envoys held discussions in Abu Dhabi and Moscow regarding potential peace talks, agreeing to include wider post-Cold War European security arrangements. European Union leaders, including diplomatic chief Kaja Kallas, cautioned against Russian traps and insisted on prioritizing an immediate ceasefire.
articles.description: Kyiv's forces are using drones and ground robots to help defend against Russia's army along the about 1,200-km front line snaking down eastern and southeastern Ukraine

articles.headline: Armed men kill 37 civilians in western Niger ambush
articles.title: Armed men kill at least 37 civilians in western Niger, say local sources
articles.summary: Armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger on November 12, 2026, according to local sources. The attack targeted villagers travelling to a market in Tera within the Tillaberi region. The dead included members of a local self defence group and residents. Conflict monitors note the region is a jihadist violence epicentre.
articles.description: Ruled by a military junta since a 2023 coup, Niger is battling violence by jihadists linked to Al-Qaeda and the Islamic State group. Thousands have been killed in the violence over the last decade

articles.headline: Francophone summit opens in Cambodia amid Rwanda and DRC leadership rift
articles.title: Francophone summit opens in Cambodia amid Rwanda-DR Congo rift
articles.summary: Delegates representing the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie gathered in Phnom Penh for a three-day meeting overshadowed by a dispute between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda. The disagreement centers on the election for secretary-general, where incumbent Louise Mushikiwabo faces opposition due to regional conflicts. The DRC threatened to exit the association if she secures a third four-year term.
articles.description: Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda clash over who should lead the organisation of French-speaking nations.

articles.headline: Lakshya Sen beats Koki Watanabe to win Kumamoto Masters Japan Open
articles.title: Lakshya Sen beats Koki Watanabe to win Kumamoto Masters Japan Open
articles.summary: Eighth-seeded Indian shuttler Lakshya Sen secured his second consecutive BWF Tour title by defeating home favorite Koki Watanabe 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 in the Kumamoto Masters Japan final. The victory earns World No. 13 Sen 9,200 points, lifting him to sixth place in the Race to Finals standings and securing a provisional qualifying spot for the BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou.
articles.description: After losing the first game, Sen, the world No. 13, bounced back in the next two games to win the contest 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 in an hour and four minutes

articles.headline: Car bombings in Russia injure former Ukrainian adviser and kill military officer
articles.title: Car bombings in Russia kill military officer, injure ex-Ukraine PM adviser
articles.summary: A car bombing in Moscow critically injured Sergei Zavorotnyi, an adviser to former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, after an explosive device detonated remotely under his vehicle on November 13, 2026. This followed a similar attack in St Petersburg that killed a Russian military serviceman. According to Al Jazeera reporting from Moscow, Russia’s Investigative Committee launched criminal inquiries into both incidents, with authorities attributing the coordinated attacks to Ukrainian orchestration.
articles.description: Moscow blames Kyiv for a series of car bombings that have targeted people linked to the war with Ukraine.

articles.headline: Putin pushes for European security overhaul during peace talks with US envoys
articles.title: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin demanded a new European security architecture during discussions with United States envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, seeking to roll back North Atlantic Treaty Organization infrastructure from Central and Eastern Europe. The Kremlin's renewed stance aims to alter post-Cold War security arrangements, alarming European leaders who fear exclusion. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drone attacks continue to target Russian infrastructure despite ongoing diplomatic efforts to broker a peace agreement.
articles.description: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Baby dies from cold in Gaza
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Baby dies from cold in Gaza
articles.description: A baby dies from the cold in Gaza as 53 countries urge Israel to allow aid in.

articles.headline: Video shows moment of Brooklyn building collapse from inside
articles.title: Video shows moment of Brooklyn building collapse from inside
articles.description: Newly released nanny cam footage shows the moment an apartment building collapsed in Brooklyn as children played inside.

articles.headline: Zimbabwe faces public health challenge in sustaining HIV prevention among youth
articles.title: Zimbabwe’s HIV gains face a test among young people
articles.summary: Public health advocates in Zimbabwe warn that decades of progress against HIV are facing challenges as some young people underestimate virus risks despite available prevention tools like pre-exposure prophylaxis. According to Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and AIDS estimates, national annual new infections dropped significantly between 2010 and 2023, yet experts emphasize the ongoing need for engaging youth effectively amid regional funding pressures.
articles.description: New prevention tools offer hope, but reaching young people remains a challenge.

articles.headline: Prime minister inaugurates planetarium and praises space progress in Mysuru
articles.title: Science must serve society, improve lives, says Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Mysuru
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the COSMOS Mysuru LED Dome Planetarium in Mysuru on November 13, 2026, stating that science must serve society and improve lives. Modi highlighted India's achievements in space exploration, including Chandrayaan-3 and Aditya-L1, and noted that opening the space sector created new opportunities. He also stressed the importance of nurturing scientific temper among students through Atal Tinkering Labs across the country.
articles.description: Emphasising the need to translate scientific innovations into practical applications that improve people’s lives, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said India was making rapid strides in space science and technology, creating new opportunities for young scientists and researchers

articles.headline: India reports 29.9 percent increase in October exports alongside narrowing deficit
articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.summary: India achieved an increase in total exports reaching 89.99 billion dollars in October, up from 69.27 billion dollars recorded in the previous year, according to official government data released on November 13, 2026. The country experienced a trade deficit of 20.09 billion dollars during the month, while total imports rose to 110.07 billion dollars compared with 94.42 billion dollars previously.
articles.description: The growth in India’s merchandise exports in October, the fastest in five years and faster than import growth, indicates that volumes of exports are growing along with prices

articles.headline: Turkiye and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement
articles.title: Turkiye and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement
articles.summary: Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan's office announced that Turkiye and Qatar have signed a mutual defence agreement following a meeting in Istanbul on Friday between Erdogan and Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani. The Turkish presidency stated the pact will enhance bilateral relations, though specific details about the accord were not immediately released.
articles.description: The pact was signed after ​the President met Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim ‌‌bin Hamad ​Al Thani in Istanbul on ⁠⁠Friday.

articles.headline: Telangana Women's Commission probes ART centres over illegal oocyte racket
articles.title: Telangana Women’s Commission issues notices to eight ART centres in illegal oocyte racket case
articles.summary: The Telangana State Women's Commission initiated an inquiry into an alleged illegal egg donation racket on November 13, 2026, issuing notices to eight Assisted Reproductive Technology centres. Chairperson Nerella Sharada expressed dissatisfaction with institutional representation and questioned claims that ninety percent of donors were voluntary and unremunerated, prompting discussions on strengthening regulatory oversight with health officials.

articles.headline: European leaders debate representation in Russia-Ukraine peace talks
articles.title: EU agrees on five countries to represent Europe in Ukraine peace talks
articles.summary: Leaders of the twenty-seven European Union member states met at a summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday to discuss how the continent should be represented in ongoing negotiations between Washington, Kyiv, and Moscow. While figures like European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and European Council President Antonio Costa are contenders, European officials remain divided on whether to send a single envoy or a team.
articles.description: European leaders believe a US-backed process will allow Moscow and Washington to decide the fate of the conflict.

articles.headline: Severe drought stunts cotton crops in Beed district of Maharashtra
articles.title: Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises
articles.summary: Stunted cotton plants and a complete lack of rain have devastated the four-acre field belonging to the Chauhan family in Majalgaon, located within the Beed district of Maharashtra. Vanita Chauhan is forced to spend her days searching for the few surviving bolls under the intense October heat, as published on November 15, 2026.
articles.description: Drought has devastated Maharashtra’s Beed district, pushing women farmers and labourers towards distress migration. Despite repeated pleas for employment, villagers say government job guarantees have failed them, even as the State announces a ₹6,728-crore package

articles.headline: Security forces arrest three militants for extortion across Manipur districts
articles.title: 3 militants arrested for extortion in Manipur
articles.summary: Security forces in Manipur apprehended three militants across the Bishnupur and Imphal East districts on November 12 and 13, 2026, for alleged extortion activities. Officials stated that two suspects belonged to the banned Kangleipak Communist Party (Apunba), while the third was linked to the United National Liberation Front (Pambei) faction, which previously signed a 2023 peace pact.
articles.description: UNLF (Pambei) signed a peace pact with the Centre and state government in 2023. However, its members allegedly continue with illegal activities, including extortion and arms possession, leading to their arrests

articles.headline: Bus collision with truck kills 24 people in Assam
articles.title: At least 24 killed after bus collides with truck in north-east India
articles.summary: At least 24 people died and 11 others were injured after a bus collided with a truck in Assam, north-east India, near Kaziranga National Park. Assam rural development minister Atul Bora stated several victims were college students. Witnesses reported one vehicle may have been speeding before the crash. The injured were admitted to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.
articles.description: Several of the deceased are college students, according to local official Atul Bora, but they have not yet been publicly identified.

articles.headline: Fossil fuel transition coalition prepares new plans without Colombia
articles.title: Coalition to move away from fossil fuels presses ahead without Colombia, its original champion
articles.summary: An international coalition promoting the transition away from fossil fuels is set to unveil new national road maps at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. The initiative is advancing led by Ireland and Tuvalu following the withdrawal of founding member Colombia, whose new government has prioritized expanding the domestic oil and gas industry.
articles.description: The coalition, launched in the Colombian coastal city of Santa Marta in April, is expected to release a progress report this week outlining steps taken by participating countries, including additional national plans to reduce dependence on coal, oil and gas

articles.headline: FAA administrator expects U.S. air travel recovery by end of November 15
articles.title: U.S. air travel should recover from ground stop by end of November 15, FAA says
articles.summary: Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford stated that nationwide air travel should fully recover by the end of November 15, 2026, following a four-hour ground stop caused by equipment overloads. Thousands of flights faced cancellations and delays across the United States. Officials including Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy attributed the incident to outdated infrastructure rather than new artificial intelligence systems.
articles.description: New technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated equipment and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the flight shutdown of more than four hours, Trump administration officials said

articles.headline: British author M John Harrison expresses despair after winning Booker Prize
articles.title: M. John Harrison | From rebellion to despair
articles.summary: British writer M John Harrison stated he has lost hope for humanity after winning the Booker Prize for his dystopian novel The End of Everything. The author previously supported the global environmental movement Extinction Rebellion in 2019. Born in 1945, Harrison moved to London from Warwickshire early in his career to pursue professional writing despite facing financial difficulties.
articles.description: The British author who won this year’s Booker Prize has long championed resistance to the status quo, but his latest novel reflects a deepening pessimism about humanity and its future

articles.headline: Climate finance sparks renewed debate at United Nations summit in Antalya
articles.title: Why climate finance remains a recurring flashpoint at UN summits
articles.summary: Negotiators gathered in Antalya, Türkiye, for the annual United Nations climate summit in November 2026, where arguments over climate finance resurfaced. Wealthy nations highlighted rising funding sums, while developing countries questioned how much money reached them and how quickly. For India and the Global South, the dispute involves protecting farms and cities from extreme weather while expanding cleaner power infrastructure and jobs affordably.
articles.description: As climate negotiators meet in Türkiye, the familiar battle over climate finance exposes a deeper divide. While wealthy nations count the money they mobilise, developing countries question how much actually reaches them

articles.headline: Anthropic prepares for massive initial public offering amid financial commitments
articles.title: Anthropic’s valuation can’t secure its moat
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic is preparing for a public offering at a valuation approaching one trillion dollars, according to financial disclosures filed in November 2026. The company faces massive computing infrastructure spending commitments totaling roughly nine hundred billion dollars through 2045, while industry analysts debate whether artificial intelligence firms can maintain sustainable competitive advantages.
articles.description: Its engineers need to keep building progressively more capable models; the AI firm has also not established that it will be able to sustain its profitability after honouring its infra commitments

articles.headline: Caretaker Israeli government weighs military action against Iran amid opposition
articles.title: Can Netanyahu launch a strike on Iran before he leaves?
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's caretaker government is considering military action against Iran despite opposition from the United States, military officials, and political rivals. While interim cabinets retain legal authority to wage war, critics warn of political motives as Netanyahu attempts to remain in power following inconclusive parliamentary elections and ongoing coalition negotiations led by opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot.
articles.description: PM's caretaker government can legally go to war, though it would likely inflame domestic divisions.

articles.headline: Ukraine reports record Russian casualties as peace talks take place
articles.title: Ukraine claims record 3,000 Russian casualties in one day as war drags on
articles.summary: Ukraine reported a record 2,980 Russian casualties on November 9, 2026, amid ongoing peace talks in Abu Dhabi involving Russian, Ukrainian, and United States delegations. articles.summary: Delhi registered an overall Air Quality Index of 403 on Friday morning, moving the metropolitan area into the severe pollution category according to Central Pollution Control Board data. The deterioration also affected surrounding north Indian locations such as Ballabgarh, Noida, and Gurugram. Meteorological factors and regional seasonal stubble burning contributed to the spike in hazardous air conditions.
articles.description: The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 403 (severe) at 9 a.m. on November 13, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data

articles.headline: West Bengal opposition forms platform to protect voters' rights
articles.title: Opposition parties, civil rights groups come together to save voters’ rights in West Bengal
articles.summary: Opposition parties and civil rights groups in West Bengal announced a joint platform on November 14, 2026, to address the unlawful deletion of over 91 million voters during a recent electoral revision. The coalition scheduled a mass convention in Kolkata on November 21 to question the Election Commission of India regarding millions of pending appeals and tribunal delays.
articles.description: The new platform calls for a mass convention in Kolkata on November 21, invites other parties and people whose names were ‘unlawfully’ removed from electoral rolls to take part

articles.headline: TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee appears at Kolkata police station for questioning
articles.title: Police question Abhishek Banerjee for three hours over post against CEC
articles.summary: Trinamool Congress national general secretary and Member of Parliament Abhishek Banerjee visited the Bhowanipur police station in Kolkata on November 14, 2026, for police questioning. The questioning relates to a first information report registered on May 27 following a complaint alleging that his social media post during the assembly election period targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Gujaratis. The politician faces an additional summons from the Girish Park police station scheduled for November 20.
articles.description: An FIR was registered against the TMC MP following a complaint about his social media post in May that allegedly targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Gujaratis during the Assembly poll period

articles.headline: Pope Leo meets clergy abuse survivors in Peru amid calls for justice
articles.title: Pope Leo meets clergy abuse survivors in Peru amid calls for justice
articles.description: Pope Leo met six clergy abuse survivors in Peru, while hundreds more say they remain excluded as they seek justice.

articles.headline: Doctor arrested for allegedly harassing house surgeon in Nedumangad
articles.title: Doctor held for ‘sexually harassing’ house surgeon in Keralam
articles.summary: Police took a government doctor into custody following allegations that he made sexual advances toward a postgraduate house surgeon at Nedumangad Government Taluk Hospital. Keralam Health Minister K Muraleedharan stated that strict disciplinary measures will be implemented against the accused. The arrest occurred at the suspect residence following the recording of the victim detailed statement and subsequent protests by workers.
articles.description: Health Minister promises action in the incident

articles.headline: UNRWA funding cuts worsen hardship for Palestinian refugees
articles.title: UNRWA funding cuts deepen hardship for Palestinian refugees in Lebanon
articles.summary: Severe funding shortfalls have forced the United Nations Relief and Works Agency to curtail vital operations across Lebanon, leaving thousands of Palestinian refugees facing diminished healthcare and overcrowded classrooms. The budgetary crisis stems primarily from ongoing United States funding freezes. Consequently, camp residents contend with deepening economic precarity, reduced educational access, and heightened social vulnerabilities.
articles.description: Funding cuts and Israel's war have left Palestinians in Lebanon in increasingly dire circumstances.

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu pushes for conflict with Iran to secure political survival
articles.title: Iranophobia: Netanyahu’s bid to transform fear into political survival
articles.summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly pressing for renewed military strikes against Iran as his right-wing coalition government loses its grip on power. Analysts and opposition leaders, including Gadi Eisenkot, claim Netanyahu is attempting to manufacture a regional crisis for his own political survival despite military warnings from figures like Eyal Zamir.
articles.description: Despite knowing a war with Iran would be manufactured for Netanyahu's survival, many would still rally behind it.
